With the proliferation of AI-generated images, digital watermarking has become an essential safeguard for protecting intellectual property and mitigating malicious exploitation. Recent works on semantic watermarking have enabled efficient copyright protection for diffusion models. However, the dependence of semantic watermarking on diffusion inversion for watermark detection creates a critical vulnerability. Imprint removal and forgery attacks exploit this weakness to produce deceptive results. Our analysis reveals that these attacks succeed by displacing watermarked latents into the unwatermarked region, while guiding unwatermarked latents into the watermarked region. Based on that, we propose Progressive Guided Inversion and Denoising (PGID), the first plug-and-play, training-free noise extraction framework designed to defend against both attack strategies. PGID effectively defends by projecting perturbed latents back to the region where they originally belong. The projection is achieved by eliminating intermediate latent deflections and mitigating adversarial perturbations through progressive inversion-denoising cycles. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple schemes demonstrate that PGID successfully restores detection reliability by recovering removed watermarks and identifying forged instances.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Code available at https://github.com/MinhQDuong/PGID
♻ ☆ BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks
Yong Wang, Kecheng Zheng, Xing Zhu, Chao Xu, Yujun Shen, Shengze Cai
Bimanual manipulation with dexterous hands has attracted growing attention in research on robotic action models. However, few studies have developed benchmarks specifically tailored for dexterous manipulation, leaving the dexterous manipulation capabilities of existing models insufficiently characterized. In this paper, we present BiDex-100, a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that combines broad task coverage, multi-dimensional evaluation, and high-DoF hand embodiments. Concretely, the benchmark comprises 106 tasks organized along five capability axes: generalization, instruction following, limited demonstrations, long horizon, and memory. Each task is paired with an out-of-domain variant featuring controlled visual and spatial changes, allowing systematic assessment of robustness. In addition, the benchmark supports two embodiments and provides 8,080 success-validated teleoperated demonstrations, totaling 6.25 million frames. We evaluate seven recent Vision-Language-Action models under a unified protocol, establishing baselines for capability-specific performance, robustness, and data efficiency. The website is available at https://robbyant-research.github.io/BiDex-100/.
♻ ☆ Label-free cell counting and viability prediction with brightfield imaging and deep learning
Amir Reza Vazifeh, Christian Zeigler, Sornanathan Meyyappan, Richard Jeske, Jason W. Fleischer
Cell viability assessment is a core requirement in cell culture systems, with critical applications in biopharmaceutical manufacturing and drug development. Conventionally, it is measured by adding membrane-impermeable dyes to a sample (a process called staining), which allows compromised cell membranes to be distinguished from intact ones. However, staining has several limitations: (a) chemical agents can perturb normal cellular processes of the cells being measured, (b) it is often ambiguous to assign viability to individual cells whose membrane integrity is only partially compromised, (c) photobleaching can undermine measurement accuracy over time when using fluorescent stains, and (d) staining cannot be performed in situ or in real time. Here, we show that (1) stained cells captured under brightfield imaging contain sufficient information to distinguish live and dead cells, and (2) cells captured under unstained brightfield imaging exhibit similar image features to their stained counterparts, enabling models trained on stained cells to generalize to unstained ones. We then report the development and validation of ViabiLens, an AI-assisted software tool for label-free cell viability analysis. ViabiLens combines a cell detection model for localizing individual cells with a convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier for live/dead prediction, paired with an interactive UMAP-based viewer for visualizing and exploring individual cells across the sample. Evaluated on Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells spanning a wide range of viability conditions, ViabiLens achieves a mean absolute error of 2.33\% on unstained samples against fluorescence-based reference measurements. The demo of ViabiLens software is available at https://amirrezavazifeh.github.io/ViabiLens-Project-Page/.
♻ ☆ HiAP: A Multi-Granular Stochastic Auto-Pruning Framework for Vision Transformers
Andy Li, Aiden Durrant, Milan Markovic, Georgios Leontidis
Vision Transformers require significant computational resources and memory bandwidth, severely limiting their deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Most structured pruning methods reduce theoretical cost effectively, yet they typically operate at a single structural granularity and depend on multi-stage pipelines with importance ranking, auxiliary solvers or post-hoc magnitude thresholding, followed by a separate fine-tuning phase to recover accuracy. We propose Hierarchical Auto-Pruning (HiAP), which casts ViT pruning as a single budget-aware learning problem and jointly allocates sparsity across four granularities in one end-to-end phase. HiAP introduces stochastic Gumbel-Sigmoid gates at macro level (attention heads and FFN blocks) and micro level (intra-head dimensions and FFN neurons), and trains them against the task loss together with an analytical MAC cost term. Two penalty weights set how much compute is removed, while the gates gradually harden into a dense, smaller sub-network at convergence. It does not require importance heuristics, ranking metrics, auxiliary solvers or secondary fine-tuning. On ImageNet, HiAP compresses DeiT-Base to 7.4G MACs at 80.88% top-1 80.40% at 7.8G without distillation and DeiT-Small to 3.1G at 79.33%, competitive with substantially more complex pipelines at matched compute. The structurally pruned network can be accelerated natively on stock kernels, and more than 90% of the theoretical MAC reduction is realized as measured throughput at batch 256 on an A100.

♻ ☆ LoBE-GS: Load-Balanced and Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Scene Reconstruction WACV 2027
Sheng-Hsiang Hung, Ting-Yu Yen, Wei-Fang Sun, Simon See, Shih-Hsuan Hung, Hung-Kuo Chu
3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has established itself as an efficient representation for real-time, high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction. However, scaling 3DGS to large and unbounded scenes such as city blocks remains difficult. Existing divide-and-conquer methods alleviate memory pressure by partitioning the scene into blocks and training on multiple, non-communicating GPUs, but introduce new bottlenecks: (i) partitions suffer from severe load imbalance since uniform or heuristic splits do not reflect actual computational demands, and (ii) coarse-to-fine pipelines fail to exploit the coarse stage efficiently, often reloading the entire model and incurring high overhead. In this work, we introduce LoBE-GS, a Load-Balanced and Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting framework, that re-engineers the large-scale 3DGS pipeline. Specifically, LoBE-GS introduces a load-balanced KD-tree scene partitioning scheme with optimized cutlines that balance per-block camera counts. To accelerate preprocessing, it employs depth-based back-projection for fast camera assignment, reducing processing time from hours to minutes. It further reduces training cost through two lightweight techniques: visibility cropping and selective densification. On large-scale urban and outdoor datasets, LoBE-GS reduces scene-partitioning time by up to an order of magnitude and worst-block fine-training time by up to $3.2\times$ relative to CityGaussian. It also substantially reduces end-to-end and post-coarse training time under matched GPU budgets while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality. LoBE-GS thus provides a communication-free alternative with favorable quality-efficiency trade-offs. The associated code is available at: https://github.com/Sunnyhong0326/lobe-gs
comment: WACV 2027. Project Page: https://sunnyhong0326.github.io/lobe-gs/
♻ ☆ Detection of trade in products derived from threatened species using machine learning and a smartphone application
Ritwik Kulkarni, WU Hanqin, Enrico Di Minin
Illegal and unsustainable wildlife trade remains a major conservation challenge and is increasingly shifting to online marketplaces where monitoring is difficult. To address this gap, we used real-world images from online platforms, enforcement seizures, and market inspections to develop a deep-learning object detection framework to identify products derived from three highly traded species: elephant, pangolin, and tiger. Our dataset of 39,941 images included both wildlife products and visually similar non-wildlife items, reflecting real enforcement complexity. We used cross-entropy and asymmetric focal loss functions to train Faster Region-based convolutional neural network (Faster R-CNN) models and compared species-specific and multispecies training strategies. The best-performing model, trained with cross-entropy on all species combined, achieved an overall accuracy of 84.2%, with high performance for pangolin (93.6%) and tiger (90.3%) and moderate performance for elephant (71.1%). Although asymmetric focal loss increased recall, it substantially reduced precision. We deployed the optimized model in a prototype smartphone application, potentially usable in real-world settings for monitoring online images. With an independent test set, the application achieved 91.3% accuracy and an F-score of 0.86. These results demonstrate the potential of object detection models to support scalable, real-time monitoring of wildlife trade and enable the rapid triage of suspicious posts, regulatory compliance, and conservation decision-making.
♻ ☆ DIP-CAD: A Design-Intent-Preserving Agent Harness for Parametric CAD Modeling
Xi Cheng, Chenxi Zhai, Hang Cheng, Mingyu Fan, Pingfa Feng, Long Zeng
Parametric CAD modeling requires not only matching the target shape, but also preserving design intent under parameter edits. However, most existing methods focus on improving static shape generation accuracy, while the dependencies that govern later edits are often overlooked. To tackle this issue, we present DIP-CAD, a design-intent-preserving agent harness for generating parametric CAD models from images. DIP-CAD combines vision-language model reasoning with CAD kernel operations to establish dependencies that encode the design intent. In parametric CAD, these dependencies are mainly established through geometry references in modeling commands and constraints in parametric sketches. At the command level, ID-based explicit geometry reference binds modeling commands to selected faces, edges, or vertices. At the sketch level, a local-coordinate bridge ensures accurate sketch placement, providing the basis for correctly establishing sketch constraints. Constraints among sketch primitives and constraints to external projected geometry further preserve both internal sketch relationships and dependencies on existing geometry. To provide a more comprehensive data foundation for parametric CAD modeling tasks, we introduce the Geometry Explicit Reference Dataset (GERD), whose structured data format links stepwise modeling commands to intermediate CAD models through explicit geometry references. On GERD-EVL and a DeepCAD test subset, DIP-CAD improves mIoU for static model generation by 11.1% and 5.6%, respectively. In parameter-editing evaluations, the corresponding mIoU improvements are 7.0% and 4.2%. Case studies further demonstrate how parameter edits drive shape updates while preserving design intent.
♻ ☆ OctWorld: Long-Range World-Consistent Video Generation with Octree-Based 3D Mapping ECCV 2026
Zelong Lv, Sicheng Xu, Jianfeng Xiang, Ruicheng Wang, Yue Dong, Yu Deng, Guangzhong Sun, Jiaolong Yang
We present OctWorld, a video diffusion framework with persistent 3D memory for generating explorable, world-consistent, and high-fidelity visual scenes. Given a single image, OctWorld performs stable autoregressive world generation along user-specified camera trajectories. We focus on long-range generation, characterized by extended camera paths and wide viewpoint coverage, where preserving spatial consistency is particularly challenging when previously generated regions are revisited. To address this problem, we introduce OctMap, an extensible and spatially adaptive 3D memory that progressively fuses generated visual observations and their corresponding depth maps into a global representation. OctMap employs TSDF fusion within a dynamic sparse octree whose spatial resolution adapts to image evidence. This design preserves geometric and appearance details across diverse scene scales while maintaining low memory overhead. Experiments demonstrate that OctWorld generates long-range, spatially consistent videos and outperforms prior methods on both existing benchmarks and challenging long-range generation settings. OctMap also provides clear advantages over point-based caches and fixed-resolution TSDF volumes. Project page: https://github.com/microsoft/OctWorld
comment: Published at ECCV 2026. Project page: https://microsoft.github.io/OctWorld/. Code: https://github.com/microsoft/OctWorld
♻ ☆ ToPO: Token-Oriented Preference Optimization for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
Juntao Xu, Shihong Li, Hoi Fan Au, Ning Zhu
Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in text-to-image generation, yet aligning their outputs with human preferences remains challenging. Diffusion-DPO learns from image preference pairs, but their global labels do not specify how supervision should be allocated across spatial locations and denoising timesteps. The semantic roles of prompt tokens are also not explicitly considered when assigning these local weights. To address these limitations, we propose Token-Oriented Preference Optimization (ToPO), which builds a token-conditioned spatial-temporal weighting map for each pair. A frozen reference denoiser obtains spatial and temporal weights from local noise-prediction error differences under shared noise, while preferred-branch cross-attention links spatial evidence to content tokens. The map reweights Diffusion-DPO and supports an auxiliary pixel-midpoint ordering loss. It requires neither local preference annotations nor a separately trained reward model. Extensive experiments across multiple preference and compositional evaluations show that ToPO achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods with only 500 training updates, demonstrating the potential of token-conditioned preference allocation for high-quality diffusion alignment within a limited update budget.
comment: 28 pages, 11 figures. Revised manuscript with updated presentation and analyses
♻ ☆ MUMINS: Metadata-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Medical Image Next-state Synthesis
Anna Oliveras, Roger Marí, Rafael Redondo, Oriol Guardià, Cynthia Ifeyinwa Ugwu, Ana Tost, Bhalaji Nagarajan, Carolina Migliorelli, Vicent Ribas, Petia Radeva
Forecasting anatomical changes such as tumor growth and neurodegeneration is a challenging generative vision task. Morphological evolution is subtle relative to static anatomy, highly patient-specific, and inherently stochastic. Existing methods struggle with several issues: deterministic networks ignore biological stochasticity, while standard diffusion models require computationally prohibitive multi-pass sampling to quantify uncertainty. We propose MUMINS (Metadata-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Medical Image Next-state Synthesis), an efficient diffusion framework that jointly diffuses a baseline scan and its follow-up residual, summed to synthesize the follow-up scan, while concurrently predicting a spatial uncertainty map, in a single reverse diffusion process. Conditioned on the time interval and relevant metadata, it preserves fine-grained anatomy by dynamically re-injecting the baseline as a soft anchor at every denoising step, and a negative-log-likelihood head learns the uncertainty map to explicitly flag error-prone regions. Designed without organ-specific heuristics, the same architecture is reused across anatomies via separate, dataset-specific retraining. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that dataset-specific retraining of MUMINS matches or outperforms dedicated, domain-specific state-of-the-art methods on lung CT (PNG) and brain MRI (OASIS-3). Project page: https://aolivtous.github.io/publications/mumins.html.

♻ ☆ K-CLUE: A Segmentation-to-Clustering Framework for Ki67 Cell Typing BMVC 2026
Ana Beatriz Vieira, Sara P. Oliveira, Diana Montezuma, João Fraga, Jaime S. Cardoso, Arlindo L. Oliveira
Ki67 is a key marker of tumor proliferation in breast cancer, but its quantification from immunohistochemistry images normally depends on supervised classifiers trained per dataset. We examine the role of frozen pretrained visual representations in annotation-free Ki67 cell typing. To this end, we use K-CLUE, a framework that segments individual nuclei, represents each nucleus with a pretrained encoder, reduces the resulting embeddings with principal component analysis, and separates Ki67-positive from Ki67-negative nuclei using k-means clustering, without task-specific training or manual annotations. Clustering the raw components is highly sensitive to the choice of encoder: across seven encoders, the Ki67-positive F1-score on matched MIST nuclei varies by 44 points, although Ki67 status remains linearly decodable from every representation, with supervised probe AUCs above 0.98. Analysis of the embedding spaces shows that clustering succeeds when DAB-related variation occupies the leading directions of variance. Whitening the retained principal components removes this dependence, reducing the spread across encoders to 1.00 F1-score point. Handcrafted color representations are also competitive, confirming that Ki67 status is strongly reflected in chromatic information, but they require an explicit choice of color space. In end-to-end evaluation, K-CLUE reaches F1-scores of 85.00% and 81.91% for Ki67-positive and Ki67-negative nuclei on MIST, and 79.59% and 81.16% on BCData, outperforming DeepLIIF and IHCScoreGAN on both datasets. These results show that pretrained representations can support annotation-free Ki67 typing when their variance structure is accounted for.
comment: Accepted at the BD-MedVis Workshop, BMVC 2026
♻ ☆ UltraFlash: Accelerating Megapixel Visual Synthesis NeurIPS 2026
Phuc Lai, Anh Nguyen, Phong Nguyen, Anh Tran
Megapixel visual synthesis with latent diffusion models requires operating far beyond the resolutions at which these models are typically trained. Cascade refinement is a leading strategy for this setting: it starts from a base image at a native resolution and progressively upsamples it to the target resolution through multiple refinement stages. Each stage typically performs a pixel-space resolution transition followed by latent-space denoising. While prior acceleration efforts mainly focus on reducing denoising cost, we identify a complementary and underexplored bottleneck: the repeated movement of representations through the VAE. We call these operations pixel-space transitions. In cascade pipelines, intermediate latents are often decoded to RGB, resized, and re-encoded before refinement, while final latents are decoded patch by patch with dense overlap to suppress boundary artifacts. We propose UltraFlash, a transition-efficient approach that accelerates these VAE-heavy operations. UltraFlash has two components. Latent Hyperloop replaces intermediate RGB round trips with a learned latent-space shortcut that approximates the decode-resize-encode transformation without repeated VAE decoding and encoding. Sparse Patch-based Decoding accelerates final reconstruction by addressing patch seams caused by inconsistent GroupNorm statistics and reusing cached statistics across patches, enabling sparse VAE decoding with much smaller overlap. Integrated into a state-of-the-art cascade baseline, UltraFlash reduces 4K generation latency by approximately 2x while improving image quality. These results show that optimizing pixel-space transitions can improve both efficiency and fidelity, offering an effective route toward fast, high-quality megapixel visual synthesis.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://qualcomm-ai-research.github.io/UltraFlash/
♻ ☆ CLEAR-IR: Clarity-Enhanced Active Reconstruction of Infrared Imagery IROS 2026
Nathan Shankar, Marton Gonczy, Hujun Yin, Pawel Ladosz
This paper presents CLEAR-IR (Clarity Enhanced Active Reconstruction of Infrared Imagery), a novel framework for enabling robust robotic perception in dark environments using active infrared (IR) sensing. IR streams are less susceptible to noise than RGB in low light conditions but are dominated by structured light emitter patterns that hinder high level tasks such as object detection, tracking, and localisation. CLEAR-IR addresses this by reconstructing clean, RGB styled images from emitter populated IR inputs using a dual stream architecture inspired by DeepMAO, enabling standard RGB trained vision pipelines to operate without visible light. Evaluation across object detection, ArUco marker detection, and visual SLAM demonstrates that CLEAR-IR produces reliable perception in conditions ranging from well lit to completely dark, where passive RGB based enhancement methods fail entirely due to the physical absence of sensor signal.
comment: Accepted and presented in IEEE/RSJ IROS 2026. Project page: https://ladoszlabs.github.io/clearir/
♻ ☆ WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
Lanxiang Hu, Yixin Huang, Abhilash Shankarampeta, Zilin Dai, Yuyuan Wu, Kun Qian, Junze Liu, Arvind Srinivasan, Mingjia Huo, Will Lin, Kai Zhong, Weiqi Zhang, Tian Wang, Qingjun Cui, Tajana Rosing, Hao Zhang
Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. We introduce WMEval, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations. By leveraging Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, we shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream applications. Spanning 9 diverse scenes, WMEval assesses action controllability, scene and character consistency, prompt adherence, kinematics, fluid mechanics, physical causality, and lighting. By executing matched action sequences in both the simulator and the world model, WMEval enables evaluation at both the perceptual level and the physical-causal level, using simulator-derived states as reference. Experiments on state-of-the-art models reveal significant room for improvement in dimensions that remain hidden by standard perceptual metrics but are vital for real-world deployments. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/WMEval.
♻ ☆ AnyCXR: Human Anatomy Segmentation of Chest X-ray at Any Acquisition Position using Multi-stage Domain Randomized Synthetic Data with Imperfect Annotations and Conditional Joint Annotation Regularization Learning
Zifei Dong, Wenjie Wu, Jinkui Hao, Tianqi Chen, Ziqiao Weng, Bo Zhou
Robust anatomical segmentation of chest X-rays (CXRs) remains challenging due to the scarcity of comprehensive annotations and the substantial variability of real-world acquisition conditions. We propose AnyCXR, a unified framework that enables generalizable multi-organ segmentation across arbitrary CXR projection angles using only synthetic supervision. The method combines a Multi-stage Domain Randomization (MSDR) engine, which generates over 100,000 anatomically faithful and highly diverse synthetic radiographs from 3D CT volumes, with a Conditional Joint Annotation Regularization (CAR) learning strategy that leverages partial and imperfect labels by enforcing anatomical consistency in a latent space. Trained entirely on synthetic data, AnyCXR achieves strong zero-shot generalization on multiple real-world datasets, providing accurate delineation of 54 anatomical structures in PA, lateral, and oblique views. The resulting segmentation maps support downstream clinical tasks, including automated cardiothoracic ratio estimation, spine curvature assessment, and disease classification, where the incorporation of anatomical priors improves diagnostic performance. These results demonstrate that AnyCXR establishes a scalable and reliable foundation for anatomy-aware CXR analysis and offers a practical pathway toward reducing annotation burdens while improving robustness across diverse imaging conditions.

♻ ☆ DeFM: Learning Foundation Representations from Depth for Robotics
Manthan Patel, Jonas Frey, Mayank Mittal, Fan Yang, Alexander Hansson, Amir Bar, Cesar Cadena, Marco Hutter
Depth sensors are widely deployed across robotic platforms, and advances in fast, high-fidelity depth simulation have enabled robotic policies trained on depth observations to achieve robust sim-to-real transfer for a wide range of tasks. Despite this, representation learning for depth modality remains underexplored compared to RGB, where large-scale foundation models now define the state of the art. To address this gap, we present DeFM, a self-supervised foundation model trained entirely on depth images for robotic applications. Using a DINO-style self-distillation objective on a curated dataset of 60M depth images, DeFM learns geometric and semantic representations that generalize to diverse environments, tasks, and sensors. To retain metric awareness across multiple scales, we introduce a novel input normalization strategy. We further distill DeFM into compact models suitable for resource-constrained robotic systems. When evaluated on depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, DeFM achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates strong generalization from simulation to real-world environments. We release all our pretrained models, which can be adopted off-the-shelf for depth-based robotic learning without task-specific fine-tuning. Webpage: https://de-fm.github.io/
comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO), 2026
♻ ☆ Amortized Set Prediction for Inverse IFS Reconstruction from Density Maps
Yutaka Yamaguti
Iterated Function Systems (IFS) generate self-similar fractals from a few contractive affine maps. The forward map from parameters to images is inexpensive and well understood, whereas the inverse problem is difficult and is typically solved by per-image optimization. We replace this loop with a single forward pass of a learned estimator that predicts the affine-map set directly from a visit-frequency density map, thereby amortizing the inverse problem. The design follows two constraints. First, density maps do not uniquely identify IFS parameters, so we evaluate by reconstruction rather than parameter recovery and handle unordered map sets by Hungarian matching. Training nevertheless matches the ground-truth parameters: reconstruction-only training gives a better one-shot output, but refinement from its predictions converges to poorer minima, whereas refinement from parameter-matched predictions keeps improving. Second, the fully known forward model lets us generate exact synthetic training pairs and supports image-only test-time refinement. On in-distribution tests, amortized initialization plus a few refinement steps gives a better quality-speed trade-off than equal-budget random-start optimization, and over 1000 steps it reaches high-quality reconstructions more often. It is robust to the sampling settings of the observation, and on an external benchmark outside its training prior it matches the mean accuracy of a recent hour-long optimizer within a minute. On real images (MNIST and Fashion-MNIST), it improves density metrics on average over a published per-image optimizer while being roughly 2 to 500 times faster per image.

♻ ☆ Procedural Exposure Bias in Skill-Augmented Language Model Agents
Qing Yang, Yuqi Xiong, Pengcheng Huang, Zhipeng Xu, Zhenghao Liu, Zulong Chen, Yu Gu, Ge Yu
External skills provide language-model agents with reusable procedural knowledge, yet how models use such knowledge after it is supplied remains poorly understood. We identify Procedural Exposure Bias (PEB), the tendency of language models to increasingly favor an action as its associated procedural pattern is repeatedly exposed in a skill, even when the interaction state and action relevance remain unchanged. We find that PEB strongly depends on how procedural knowledge is represented: presenting the same content visually substantially attenuates exposure-induced shifts in action preference relative to textual presentation. Further analysis shows that this attenuation primarily arises from visual encoding rather than structured layout. Although repeated procedural signals remain recoverable from Visual representations, they exert a weaker influence on downstream action prediction, distinguishing signal accessibility from its use as action evidence. This effect also extends to executable action selection, where increasing exposure more strongly favors the corresponding action under Text than Visual. Layer-wise analyses show that exposure-dependent action evidence becomes more pronounced toward the model output, with stronger evidence under Text, while activation interventions reveal architecture-specific roles of internal components in transmitting or counteracting the preference shift. Complete-agent evaluations across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop further show that Visual skills achieve higher macro-average task success than Text skills for all four evaluated models. These findings establish skill representation as an important factor governing how procedural knowledge is translated into agent decisions. All code is available at https://github.com/NEUIR/Vis-Skill.

♻ ☆ Single-Step Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation Using Implicit Bridge Consistency Distillation WACV27
Suhyeon Lee, Kwanyoung Kim, Jong Chul Ye
Unpaired image-to-image translation has seen significant progress since the introduction of CycleGAN. However, methods based on diffusion models or Schrödinger bridges have yet to be widely adopted in real-world applications due to their iterative sampling nature. To address this challenge, we propose Implicit Bridge Consistency Distillation (IBCD), which enables single-step bidirectional unpaired translation without using adversarial loss. IBCD reformulates consistency distillation by using a diffusion implicit bridge model that connects PF-ODE trajectories between distributions, parametrized on a signed time axis whose sign selects the target domain, so that one network translates in both directions in a single step. Additionally, we introduce two key improvements: 1) distribution matching for consistency distillation and 2) adaptive weighting method based on distillation difficulty. Experimental results demonstrate that IBCD achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets in a single generation step, and that it extends to brain MRI contrast translation.
comment: WACV27. 39 pages, 20 figures
♻ ☆ TALON: Token-Aligned Lightweight Adapters for 6-DoF Spacecraft Pose Estimation
Abid Ali, Nidhal Eddine Chenni, Arunkumar Rathinam, Djamila Aouada
Monocular 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation methods predominantly process individual frames, discarding the temporal information present in an image sequence acquired during spacecraft manoeuvres. Few temporal approaches require full backbone fine-tuning or auxiliary optical flow networks, risking catastrophic forgetting or increasing computational cost, respectively. We propose TALON (Token-Aligned Lightweight adapters for Orbital Navigation): spatiotemporal 3D adapters injected before the self-attention layers of a frozen ViT vision transformer, combined with a patch-token alignment loss that geometrically grounds the adapted features to keypoint structure through a prototype-conditioned KL-divergence objective. Pre-attention placement allows the frozen attention to reason over temporally enriched tokens, achieving stronger performance with a single adapter per block than post-attention alternatives. The alignment loss shapes the intermediate representations so that each keypoint induces a spatially precise activation in the token field, while the framework adds less than 5% parameters to the frozen backbone. On SPADES dataset, TALON reduces the pose error by 50% over the prior state-of-the-art, and on SwissCube dataset it surpasses the prior best by 21.8% in ADD-0.1d accuracy. Zero-shot cross-domain evaluation from sim-to-real on SPARK real data reduces pose error by 4.7x, and ablations characterise the role of adapter depth across in-domain and cross-domain settings.
comment: 13 pages paper with 3 figures in total
♻ ☆ Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People SIGIR 2026
Fairooz Azim, Lydia Achour, Claudia Borg, Lina Rojas-Barahona
Visual grounding (VG) in visual question answering (VQA) is a fundamental capability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), enabling the detection of the most relevant region in an image to answer the question. This reflects the model's capability of multimodal comprehension, which is crucial when interacting with visually impaired people (VIP). Indeed, visual grounding, when applied to assistive scenarios, is not merely a technical feature, but rather a trust and safety requirement. In this work, we study visual grounding in VLMs for visually impaired people. To this end, we assess open-source VLMs on visual grounding using the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset and challenge, which contains real-life images taken by VIP. We propose VG-SHAP, which extends an existing explainability framework to provide visual grounding explanations, allowing the evaluation of black-box VLMs. Our results on the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding challenge show that despite generating correct answers, VLMs struggle to ground in the proper region in the image. However, these results are constrained by the quality of the segmentation model of our explainability framework and further research is necessary.
comment: Published at the second workshop on evaluation for multimodal generation EvalMG26 @ SIGIR 2026. July 24th 2026. Melbourne Australia
♻ ☆ Metric Scale for Insta360 Structure-from-Motion from the Camera's Embedded IMU
Davide Cuttini, Diego Di Tommaso, Alessio Antoniacomi, Luca Simonetti
Structure-from-motion (SfM) from the dual-fisheye video of a consumer 360-degree camera recovers geometry only up to a similarity transform; in the pipeline considered here, metric scale is obtained from smartphone ARKit or ARCore poses captured alongside the camera. This paper evaluates a self-contained alternative: the IMU embedded in the Insta360 X5 and X6, recorded at 1 kHz. The sensor is characterised (noise density, camera-IMU synchronisation, accelerometer scale factor, bias stability), the camera-IMU rotation and frame timing are estimated from the data, and the scale is recovered by a linear visual-inertial alignment over the SfM poses of a whole survey. The standard formulation, with gravity and accelerometer bias shared across the survey, overestimates the scale by 3.4% on average; estimating each contiguous segment independently and averaging removes the bias. On nine surveys with a co-mounted LiDAR scanner the inertial scale deviates from the LiDAR by 0.81% in mean absolute error, against 1.94% for the smartphone scale; on printed fiducial markers both agree within the 1% uncertainty of the target. On the reference trajectories of thirty sequences of a public benchmark, brought to scales of 1/40, 1 and 40, the estimator recovers the metric scale with a mean error of -0.07% and a standard deviation of 1.28%. On fifty production surveys where the smartphone is the only reference, the two scales agree to a standard deviation of 2.3%, the inertial scale being 0.3% lower on average; the difference is uncorrelated with run length, grows with the extent of the smartphone anchor, and cannot be attributed to either reference. An ablation over window construction and a comparison with monocular metric-depth networks complete the study.
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/OverTheReality/OverMaps360_50
♻ ☆ Does Attention-Guided Masking Really Help Object Discovery in Object-Centric Learning? NeurIPS 2026
Youliang Tao, Yanhua Han, Bin Zhao, Juho Kannala, Joni Pajarinen, Rongzhen Zhao
Object-Centric Learning (OCL) aims to decompose images into objects without human annotations. A major family of mainstream methods uses Slot Attention to aggregate image features into object-level representations and then from them reconstructs masked image content, i.e., Random Masking (RM), to provide self-supervision. The recent method DIAS simply masks image patches at uniform randomness yet achieves competitive object discovery accuracy. Since attention during aggregation already possesses object discovery ability, we explore using it to develop a better image patch masking strategy, i.e., Attention Guided Masking (AGM), thereby providing better self-supervision. Results on six recognized datasets show that AGM does not always outperform RM. Under unconditional slot initialization, AGM substantially improves background segmentation on datasets with realistic textures (COCO and VOC); Regardless of conditional or unconditional slot initialization and across datasets, foreground object discovery remains comparable or decreases. We suggest peer researchers in the OCL community that attempts to exploit internal attention semantics to improve OCL with masked decoding are risky. Our source code, model checkpoints and evaluation logs are available on https://github.com/und-entropy/Does-Attention-Guided-Masking-Really-Help-Object-Discovery-in-Object-Centric-Learning-.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 PriGM
♻ ☆ Simulation of temporomandibular joint space changes based on rigid-body transformation using virtual and semi-virtual models
Agnieszka Anna Tomaka, Krzysztof Domino, Michał Tarnawski, Emil Kalinowski, Małgorzata Domino, Dariusz Pojda
The integration of multimodal data within a common coordinate system is essential for spatial analysis of the stomatognathic system. This study aims to develop a multimodal data integration methodology for digital modeling of spatial changes in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) across various mandible positions. A transformation tree framework was proposed to integrate CBCT, facial, and dental representation images into a common coordinate system and to simulate seven mandible positions using rigid-body transformations. Two proprietary models were applied. Spatial changes in mandible positions were propagated to TMJ articular surface positions using both models, although the results were model-related. The model-based uncertainty was quantified using error metrics. The consistency error revealed variability that dominated in the translation component over the rotation component of the rigid-body transformation, and showed anisotropy in the latero-lateral direction. The simulation errors were not uniform across mandible positions and were higher (p<0.0001) at the TMJ level (1.46 mm) than at the dental level (0.47 mm). As even small discrepancies in mandible position can lead to significant changes in the TMJ joint space, the proposed methodology may be useful for evaluating geometrically related positions of the mandible and TMJ, particularly when repeated radiographic imaging of the TMJs is undesirable.
comment: 29 pages, 6 figures
♻ ☆ SuperMotion: Source-Preserving Denoising for Text-Driven Human Motion Editing
Fa-Ting Hong, Peter Wonka
Text-driven human motion editing aims to realize a requested change while preserving compatible source content. Existing diffusion editors rely largely on learned conditioning for preservation of the unedited part, yet their outputs can lose temporal detail as denoising proceeds. We propose the \textbf{Source-Preserving Denoising framework (SuperMotion)}, which explicitly reuses the source at each reverse step for source preservation. We first align the source motion to the output timeline and predict a preservation gate that controls reuse across frames and feature dimensions. A clean-space source anchor then utilizes the learned preservation gate to blend the predicted clean motion with the aligned source and passes the corrected estimate directly to the sampling posterior. Because the aligned source is a realized motion rather than a regression output, the anchor injects sample-level temporal detail that a reconstruction-trained denoiser tends to smooth away. To learn effective source reuse, we supervise the anchored estimate against the editing target and match its second temporal differences through a temporal high-frequency loss. These objectives require no explicit edit masks. Extensive experiments show that SuperMotion improves editing accuracy, reaching 33.20\% full-pool R@1 on MotionFix, while reducing temporal-detail attenuation and preserving motion dynamics as it realizes the requested changes. Ablations confirm that the learned preservation gate is responsible for the gain and that it reuses the source to retain the unedited content properly.
comment: Project page: https://harlanhong.github.io/Projects/SuperMotion/index.html
♻ ☆ Seeing the Options: Typed Decisions over Visual Candidates with Reusable Option Memory
Fengxin Li
Agents end many steps in a typed decision over a set of candidates: which screen element to click, which product to pick. System One models answer in one forward pass, and Jeva showed that four properties the setting demands - a "none of the above" probability, invariance to candidate order, scalability in the number of candidates, and reuse of candidate computation - follow from encoding the request and each candidate separately and letting a request state read a candidate memory. Jeva is text-only, and existing multimodal System One models (OneJev, Jev-Omni) put images in the request while candidates stay text in letter slots. This paper asks what happens to the four properties, and to accuracy, when the candidates themselves are images. Iris admits image, text, or mixed candidates and leaves Jeva's decision module untouched. On a visual-candidate benchmark built from Multimodal-Mind2Web (every candidate is the element's screenshot crop, K=16, three splits), independent encoding reaches 78.4/72.1/74.8% with a flip rate of exactly zero, while joint encoding (OneJev-4B fine-tuned on the same data) reaches 90.6/89.5/91.6% but changes its answer on 8-10% of records when the crops are reordered. Most of the gap is the candidate not seeing the request: a third design that encodes each candidate after the state - but never after another candidate - keeps order invariance exactly, shares the state pass through a forked cache, and reaches 92.1/87.0/90.2% at a third of OneJev's latency with a calibrated null probability (AUROC 0.93-0.97). Letting pooled candidates see each other (set attention, token-level reads, multi-vector memory) buys nothing, because the encoder maps visually distinct elements to vectors within cosine 0.999 of each other. Reusing image candidates across requests cuts latency 37x at K=256 and 191x at K=2048. Code: https://github.com/lllfx/Iris
♻ ☆ Can One Hear Geometry? Gauge-Invariant Spectral Descriptors for Text-to-B-rep Retrieval
Hongzhu Yi, Hao Liu, Tao Yu, Tiankun Yang, Yujia Yang, Zhenghao Zhang, Tianyu Zong, Zhenyu Guan, Bingkang Shi, Haopeng Jin, Yuanxiang Wang, Zhongtian Luo, Jungang Xu
Text-to-3D solid retrieval faces a fundamental representation gap: while natural language describes intrinsic shapes, Boundary Representation (B-rep) entangles precise geometry with arbitrary variations in pose, scale, and boundary encoding conventions. Existing methods either discretize B-reps at the cost of analytic precision, or learn features from topological graphs without explicit invariance guarantees. We propose a text-to-B-rep retrieval framework based on geometric equivalence classes and spectral invariants, mathematically eliminating representation ambiguities prior to cross-modal alignment. Formalizing translation, rotation, reflection, uniform scaling, and contour re-indexing via group actions, we exploit the planar-profile-and-extrusion structure of engineering solids to construct a unified spectral descriptor across cross-sectional regions, contour boundaries, and extrusion depths. On public benchmarks, our method achieves state-of-the-art recall performance across all evaluation metrics.
♻ ☆ DyRA: Portable Dynamic Resolution Adjustment Network for Existing Detectors
Daeun Seo, Hoeseok Yang, Hyungshin Kim
Achieving constant accuracy in object detection is challenging due to the inherent variability of object sizes. One effective approach to this problem involves optimizing input resolution, referred to as a multi-resolution strategy. Previous approaches to resolution optimization have often been based on pre-defined resolutions with manual selection. However, there is a lack of study on run-time resolution optimization for existing architectures. This paper introduces DyRA, a dynamic resolution adjustment network providing an image-specific scale factor for existing detectors. This network is co-trained with detectors utilizing specially designed loss functions, namely ParetoScaleLoss and BalanceLoss. ParetoScaleLoss determines an adaptive scale factor for robustness, while BalanceLoss optimizes overall scale factors according to the localization performance of the detector. The loss function is devised to minimize the accuracy drop across contrasting objectives of different-sized objects for scaling. Our proposed network can improve accuracy across various models, including RetinaNet, Faster-RCNN, FCOS, DINO, and H-Deformable-DETR. The code is available at https://github.com/DaEunFullGrace/DyRA.git.
comment: The formulation for scaling contains unnecessary parts or marginal effects on accuracy. See our recent paper, which reformulates loss functions and corresponding explanations
♻ ☆ Look Beyond the Question: Preserve-Focus-Fuse for Whole-Slide Image Question Answering
Xiangyu Li, Jincheng Li, Tianle Du, Yanheng Li, Haoxuan Che, Yuxin Sun, Long Bai, Liangliang Liu, Ran Su
A question about a whole-slide image rarely names every morphological finding needed to answer it. Question-guided patch selection can therefore overlook supporting morphology, while slide-level compression can dilute focal evidence. Inspired by how pathologists combine broad slide review, question-directed examination, and integration of their findings, we introduce BEYONDPATH, a Preserve-Focus-Fuse framework for whole-slide image question answering. Preserve learns a question-agnostic Morphology Bank through answer supervision across multiple questions about each training slide. Focus retrieves questionspecific evidence from all foreground patches, including regions outside the Bank. Fuse integrates the preserved morphology at the retrieved evidence positions through Morphology-on-Visual-Evidence Fusion, producing a fixed 96-token visual prefix. On WSI-Bench, BEYONDPATH achieves an Avg-9 of 0.769 and leads all eight reported report-generation metrics using the same checkpoint. It also achieves 0.639 zero-shot overall accuracy on SlideBench-BCNB. Controlled ablations show complementary benefits from morphology preservation and question-directed retrieval, and support cross-question supervision and fusion at the evidence positions. These results support looking beyond the question's explicit cues: preserving broader slide morphology while retaining the ability to seek evidence for each question.
♻ ☆ A Computationally Efficient Multi-Section Whole Slide Image Analysis for Capturing Prostate Cancer Multifocality in Biochemical Recurrence Prediction
Yesung Cho, Dongmyung Shin, Sujeong Hong, Jooyeon Lee, Seongmin Park, Geongyu Lee, Won Young Park, Bongjin Park, Jongbae Park, Hong Koo Ha
Prostate cancer is among the most frequently diagnosed malignancies in men worldwide. However, precise prediction of biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy remains challenging. Here, we propose a computationally efficient multi section whole slide image analysis framework designed to capture the whole gland tumor landscape. We curated a large scale dataset comprising 23,451 slides from 789 patients and systematically optimized patch and slide sub sampling to substantially reduce the computational cost of training and inference. Under this efficient configuration, the framework achieved strong predictive performance for 1- and 2-year BCR, with discrimination and clinical net benefit comparable to or exceeding those of established clinical benchmarks. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, the AI derived risk score remained an independent prognostic factor among the covariates examined, and its integration with clinical variables further improved prognostic performance. External validation in an independent cohort provided preliminary evidence of transferability. Finally, attention-dispersion analysis showed that the model drew prognostic information from multiple sections, consistent with the multifocal nature of prostate cancer. Collectively, these findings support the potential of multi section slide analysis as a scalable approach for postoperative BCR risk assessment in prostate cancer.
♻ ☆ What Makes Video World Model Latents Action-Relevant: Prediction over Reconstruction
Jewon Yeom, Hanseul Kim, Jeongjae Park, Sungmok Jung, Jaejin Lee, Taesup Kim
Video world models are increasingly used to provide predictive visual representations, yet it remains unclear which pretraining signals induce action-relevant structure in their latent spaces. We study this question through a unified probe-based evaluation across diverse encoder families, including image-only self-supervision, video pretraining with and without latent prediction, reconstruction-based autoencoders, diffusion models, and shortcut-forcing dynamics models. Using a common inverse-dynamics probing objective, we find that action-relevant structure is driven primarily by temporal video pretraining rather than pixel reconstruction fidelity: models with strong pixel decoding quality can exhibit near-zero action recoverability, while video-pretrained self-supervised encoders consistently achieve the best Pareto trade-off between visual fidelity and action prediction. Comparing V-JEPA and VideoMAE further shows that most gains arise from natural-video temporal context, with feature-level latent prediction providing a smaller additional benefit. These trends transfer across robotic benchmarks, though CALVIN reveals that static-environment tasks can partially mask the importance of temporal structure by allowing strong image priors to suffice. Finally, inverse-dynamics supervision substantially improves robustness to visual corruption, suggesting that action-aware objectives regularize latent geometry beyond clean-setting performance. Our results identify temporal predictive structure -- not reconstruction fidelity -- as the primary ingredient underlying action-relevant video representations.

♻ ☆ Uncertainty-Guided Multimodal Consensus for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis WWW2027
Guowei Zhong, Junjie Li, Huaiyu Zhu, Ruohong Huan, Yun Pan
Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) has made considerable progress in recent years. Existing MSA methods mainly learn shared multimodal representations or train unimodal predictors with a common multimodal label. However, assigning the shared label to every modality can obscure modality-specific sentiment, while direct fusion may overemphasize unreliable predictions when modalities disagree. To address these issues, we propose Uncertainty-Guided Multimodal Consensus (UMC), which first recovers continuous unimodal pseudo-labels and then forms a reliability-aware consensus across modalities. Our method consists of two key components: i) Continuous Prototype-Guided Label Recovery (CPLR), which combines heteroscedastic predictions with ordered sentiment prototypes and uses confidence and label conflict to refine continuous unimodal pseudo-labels, and ii) Reliability and Precision Consensus (RPC), which estimates sample-dependent modality reliability from predictive statistics and cross-modal disagreement and combines it with predictive precision through a closed-form consensus solver. Extensive experiments conducted on four publicly available MSA datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed model.

☆ REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
Yuxi Huang, Silin Zhou, Chenhao Wang, Zihan Li, Gangming Guo, Pei Ke, Shen Gao, Shuo Shang
Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items. However, randomly initialized SID token embeddings and GR models trained from scratch do not directly inherit the semantic relations inherent in items, while inter-item collaborative relations are learned largely implicitly through token-level attention and next-token supervision. To address this limitation, we propose REGER, a unified framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation. We pretrain the GR model through generative semantic retrieval, enabling it to inherit inter-item semantic similarity by learning to generate semantic neighbors' SIDs. We combine global attention with local attention aligned with SID boundaries to capture historical context and directed transitions between adjacent items. We further develop a theoretical framework for hierarchical preference decomposition over the SID prefix tree, proving an exact factorization of collaborative preference distributions and a weighted decomposition of item-level KL divergence into prefix-conditional KL divergences. Building on this analysis, we distill a discriminative teacher's full conditional distributions over all legal next tokens at ground-truth prefixes along the target SID path, jointly optimizing this objective with cross-entropy. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over existing GR baselines and support the effectiveness of the proposed preference distillation.

☆ LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation ECML
Nesta Midavaine, Floris Fok, Paulo Mendes, Joao Silva, Önder Akaçık, Dimas Lima, Zülküf Genç
We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. LCM-Promo is a task-specific Large Commerce Model (LCM): a finetuned LLM trained on transactional commerce data to predict user intent and promotion response. It learns monotonic promotion-response curves from production logs by interpreting single-token outputs as conversion-threshold probabilities, while conditioning on session context such as day and delivery shift. In a production A/B test on churn reactivation, LCM-Promo increased conversion by 1% and reduced promotion cost by 6% relative to the Segment-EMA production baseline.

☆ Can Complementary Signals Bridge Similarity Islands? Manifold-Augmented Graph Embedding for Multimodal Recommendation NeurIPS 2026
Zhenye Yang, Jinpeng Chen, Wenbo Fu, Jun Ma, Huan Li, Qimin Zhou, Tao Wang, Li Sun, Senzhang Wang
Multimodal Recommender Systems (MMRS) leverage rich item features to mitigate data sparsity, yet similarity-driven graph construction and propagation can favor semantically similar substitutes over functionally related complements. When behavioral associations connect semantically distant items, complementary signals can remain geometrically isolated, yielding fragmented "Similarity Islands" and semantic drift when standard propagation is applied. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE (Manifold-Augmented Graph Embedding), a framework for personalized multimodal ranking that decouples complementarity modeling into offline geometric warping and online topological propagation. The offline phase enhances item representations by extracting complement-aware residual directions via a Soft Conceptor mechanism and injecting them under a local gap-preserving constraint, incorporating co-purchase evidence while controlling the magnitude of geometric perturbation. Synergistically, the online phase employs an asymmetric dual-stream GNN that treats visual features as stable anchors and augmented textual features as flexible probes, fused through a self-calibrated cross-modal mechanism to reconcile shared semantics and modality-specific residual cues. Extensive experiments on four Amazon datasets show that MAGE yields consistent improvements over strong multimodal recommendation baselines. Together with the supporting analyses in the appendix, these results suggest that geometry-aware augmentation can alleviate the semantic mismatch that arises in complementary recommendation settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/Alex-bupt/mage.

☆ When Is Additional Retrieval Worthwhile? A Cost-Aware Study of Evidence Gain and Answer Reliability in RAG
Zhouting Zhao
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can benefit from more sophisticated retrieval, but extra retrieval may be unnecessary for many questions and gains in evidence retrieval may not translate into faithful or correct answers. We study a cost-aware, two-action retrieval policy that chooses between a dense-retrieval-plus-reranking baseline and a hybrid lexical--dense retriever. Rather than classifying baseline retrieval as simply successful or unsuccessful, we estimate the question-specific incremental evidence-retrieval benefit of hybrid retrieval using features available before the routing decision. A regularized linear model and decision threshold are selected using document-grouped cross-validation and frozen prior to held-out evaluation. On 60 previously unseen QASPER training-split articles (188 questions, 169 evidence-evaluable), the policy triggers hybrid retrieval on 46 questions (24.5\%) and obtains the same evidence Hit@10 as always-hybrid retrieval (78.70\%, versus 76.92\% for always-keep). Paired, paper-cluster bootstrap intervals do not establish a reliable utility advantage. We further compare generated answers from a 4-bit Qwen3-4B model under the three retrieval policies. Provisional answer-level assessments show no clear correctness or faithfulness improvement after partial review, despite the evidence-retrieval result. The generation assessments remain model-assisted and lack independent human validation. These results expose an important distinction between retrieving relevant evidence efficiently and improving the reliability of the generated answer. The work is presented as a reproducible empirical study, not a claim of statistically established answer-quality superiority.
☆ LESSRec: Level-Specific History Modeling for Semantic ID-Based Recommendation
Shangxin Yang, Zongwei Wang, Jing Long, Junliang Yu, Min Gao
Semantic ID-based recommendation represents each item as a sequence of semantic tokens obtained through residual quantization. This paradigm generates the next item's tokens autoregressively from coarse to fine, entailing each prediction attending to historical tokens at all semantic levels. However, our inference-time analysis reveals that historical tokens at the target-token's semantic level tend to be more informative, whereas other levels can introduce interference. Motivated by these findings, we propose LESSRec that separately encodes the historical token sequence at each semantic level and restricts attention over historical tokens to the sequence at the target token's semantic level during prediction. To complement these level-specific histories, LESSRec explicitly provides an item-level semantic sequence that represents each historical item's overall semantics in chronological order. The decoder accesses the level-aligned token sequence and the item-level semantic sequence through two separate cross-attention branches and fuses their contexts. We further introduce LESSRec+, which uses separate encoders for different semantic-level histories with the same total parameter count to reduce encoder computation. Extensive experiments across three public datasets and three tokenizers demonstrate the recommendation effectiveness of LESSRec and LESSRec+, with efficiency analyses highlighting the computational benefits of LESSRec+.
☆ Modeling Preference Dependencies with Directed Acyclic Graphs for Narrative-Driven Recommendation
Mingzhe Lu, Jian Qin, Ruize Qin, Jinhao Liu, Yunpeng Li, Hang Su
Narrative-driven recommendation allows users to express multifaceted needs through free-form text where stated preferences naturally qualify and condition one another. Existing methods typically treat narratives as flat keyword combinations or unconstrained generative queries, failing to capture how complex preferences hierarchically refine and contextualize each other. We propose the Preference Dependency Graph Framework (PDG-F), a narrative-driven recommendation framework centered on explicit preference dependencies. Specifically, PDG-A (PDG-Agent) first parses unstructured requests to organize user preferences and their mutual qualifications into a directed acyclic Preference Dependency Graph (PDG). Through this graph, candidate evidence from the open Web is acquired via directed path retrieval, and final recommendations are determined by topological path ranking. Comprehensive experiments across three diverse domains spanning English and Chinese contexts confirm that PDG-F consistently achieves superior recommendation performance over competitive baselines, open-domain retrieval agents, and frontier language models. Further diagnostic analyses show that our dependency-guided retrieval markedly raises the attainable candidate-pool ceiling, demonstrating the fundamental value of modeling preference dependencies in narrative-driven recommendation.

☆ GradCO: Behavior-Aware Gradient-Conflict Offloading for Text-Based Person Anomaly Search
Zhiheng Fu, Zixu Li, Zhiwei Chen, Jiale Huang, Fangxu Liu, Jinhe Bi, Yupeng Hu
Text-based Person Anomaly Search (TPAS) retrieves a target pedestrian using natural-language descriptions of appearance and normal or anomalous behavior. Unlike conventional text-based person retrieval, TPAS must preserve identity cues while distinguishing fine-grained behaviors. It presents two challenges: same-identity, different-behavior hard negatives cause gradient conflict during granular alignment, while strong appearance cues can obscure weak behavioral evidence during aggregation. We propose GradCO (behavior-aware Gradient-Conflict Offloading), comprising three complementary components. Behavior-Aware Mixture-of-Experts (B-MoE) forms appearance, normal-behavior, and anomalous-behavior streams whose roles are learned from retrieval objectives without expert-specific semantic labels. Conflict Offload Learning (COL) uses pair-conditioned offload anchors in similarity computation to reduce the conflicting-gradient burden on the main text representations. Hierarchical Intent Alignment (HIA) aggregates expert similarities and features using query-conditioned weights. Experiments on five TPAS/TIPR benchmarks show GradCO significantly surpasses SOTA methods and validate our design.
☆ TaskBridge: Technical Report for SIGIR 2026 eCommerce Challenge SIGIR 2026
Zhiheng Fu, Yupeng Hu, Zixu Li, Zhiwei Chen, Qinlei Huang, Shaokun Wang, Han Liu, Fan Liu, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie
The SIGIR 2026 eCommerce Challenge Query Reformulation Task evaluates the reformulation of task-oriented queries into expressions suitable for product retrieval, followed by BM25-based retrieval. These queries often imply product needs through activity-level semantics, creating a lexical gap with catalog descriptions. Systems must preserve task intent while adapting the number of reformulations to the Automatic and Interactive protocols. We propose TaskBridge, a catalog-anchored framework comprising Catalog Semantic Anchoring, Unified Five-Candidate Rewriting, and Protocol-Aware Selection. It grounds queries in catalog vocabulary, generates five complementary reformulations, and selects one query for Automatic retrieval or up to four for Interactive retrieval using BM25 scores, query-product reranking, and weighted Jaccard overlap. The selected queries are independently executed using BM25 to produce results in the required six-column format. Experiments demonstrate improved retrieval effectiveness, with multiple complementary queries providing additional gains in the Interactive setting. TaskBridge achieved first place in the SIGIR 2026 eCommerce Challenge.

☆ AutoRSE: Evaluating LLM Agents as Recommendation Engineers for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems
Rui Tian, Yi Fang, Yejin Hua, Du Wang, Yuzhe Wang, Minxuan Shan, Zirui Ren, Xinyu Lin, Chongming Gao, Wenjie Wang, Fuli Feng
Recommender Systems Engineer Agents (RSE-Agents), which use LLM-based agents to autonomously improve recommendation algorithms, are emerging as a promising paradigm. However, their capabilities and limitations remain poorly understood due to the lack of a unified, standardized evaluation framework and systematic trajectory-level analysis. To address this gap, we introduce AutoRSE, an evaluation framework spanning six representative industrial-grade recommendation tasks, and conduct a large-scale empirical study of three frontier LLMs across three widely used agent harnesses. Our results show that RSE-Agents consistently enhance the performance of backbones on five of the six tasks, with an average relative improvement of 16.1%, indicating that they can already autonomously improve recommendation performance. However, trajectory-level analysis also reveals that current RSE-Agents function primarily as engineering optimizers rather than algorithmic improvers: their gains are largely driven by hyperparameter tuning, training strategies, and model ensembling, while genuine algorithmic innovations are rare. Since the largest gains in recommender systems often stem from algorithmic advances, this behavior underscores a fundamental limitation of current RSE-Agents. To probe this limitation, we perform idea-injection experiments and show that agents equipped with innovative ideas from frontier research or human experts achieve substantially larger improvements than those relying on self-generated ideas. These results suggest that idea generation is a central bottleneck of current RSE-Agents, highlights a key direction for the future recommendation system research. Our implementation is publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/Ray-Tiann/AutoRSE.

☆ Lossless Compression of Proximity Graph Indexes for Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search CIKM 2026
Francesco Benocci, Leonard Dahlmann, Francesco Gargiulo, Tobias Heuer, Silvio Martinico, Franco Maria Nardini, Cosimo Rulli, Rossano Venturini
Graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexes, such as HNSW, are the backbone of modern vector search. However, their massive memory footprint creates a severe infrastructure bottleneck. While vector quantization is widely adopted to reduce the memory required to store data vectors, the graph's edge structure increasingly dominates total memory usage. Compressing these adjacency lists for online search presents a critical system challenge: because decompression occurs during query processing, i.e., while navigating the graph, memory savings cannot come at the expense of query latency. In this paper, we present a compression technique explicitly tailored for live HNSW routing. By applying offline graph permutations to artificially induce structural locality, we enable the use of SIMD-accelerated integer compressors, such as Stream VByte, for rapid on-the-fly decompression. Evaluated across diverse real-world workloads, we significantly outperform the current state of the art in both compression ratio and query latency. Our experimental results show that we achieve compression ratios up to 52.7% with negligible penalties in latency compared to the uncompressed baseline. Furthermore, our technique has been effectively deployed in production at eBay, achieving up to 44.3% reduction in edge storage with no degradation in query latency.

☆ Coverage Under Contradiction: A Benchmark for Negation-Aware Retrieval CIKM 2026
Pasha Abrishamchian, Eugene Yang, Andrew Yates, Nazli Goharian, Ophir Frieder
Coverage-evaluation benchmarks quantify whether retrieved evidence covers the different pieces of information needed to satisfy an information need. Existing benchmarks mostly consider factual claims that may already be known to pretrained retrieval components, leaving open whether retrievers find corpus evidence when it contradicts those priors. We study how retrievers behave when their parametric knowledge and the information in a corpus disagree. To do so, we develop a process to augment a nugget-based coverage benchmark with controlled contradictions. For each nugget, we create a negated counterpart and edit its supporting documents to support that negation while preserving the context. Applying this process to CoverageBench, a benchmark measuring information coverage, we create CoverageBench-Negate, spanning six datasets and roughly 63,000 original-edited evidence pairs (one per nugget-document link). We attach rich construction metadata to every pair and additionally provide out-of-family LLM judgments over all pairs and a human audit of a sample. In baseline experiments, BM25 separates original from edited near-twin evidence substantially better than dense retrievers (Qwen3 and Jina), which stay near chance. We release the benchmark on Hugging Face Datasets (nuggets, documents, pairs) together with the construction materials, including the prompts used to create it.

☆ Rethinking Positional Encoding and Interaction Granularity for CTR Prediction
Xinxun Zhang, Yuxiang Wang, Xiaokai Zhou, Jiayue Li, Yi Li, Yue Liu, Jun Zhang, Xiaoling Zhou, Tieyun Qian, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang
Click-through rate (CTR) prediction relies on historical behaviors and contextual features to estimate clicks on a target item. Existing Transformer-based CTR models often adopt index-based or temporal positional encodings and token-level causal interaction. However, we observe that most existing positional encodings do not outperform NoPE, while relaxing causal constraints within target-relative temporal groups also yields gains. These observations motivate a fundamental question: what positional encoding and interaction granularity does CTR prediction actually require? To address this question, we propose \textbf{TRIP}, which combines target-aware rank--time positional encoding with temporal-group interaction modeling. Specifically, Factorized Rank Encoding represents each behavior's ordinal position within the historical sequence through a low-rank factorization, while Target-Relative Time Encoding characterizes its temporal distance to the target on a coarse-to-fine scale. This joint design grounds each behavior's positional representation in its sequence context and temporal relation to the current target. Furthermore, Temporal Group-Causal Interaction enriches intra-group representations through bidirectional interaction and masked reconstruction while preserving inter-group causal order. Finally, behavior representations are condensed into compact group summaries for efficient group-level modeling in subsequent layers. Experiments on four public benchmarks show that TRIP improves AUC by up to 4.45\% relative to the strongest baseline.

☆ Tessera: Structure-Completed Evidence Units for Web Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Peichun Hua, He Sun, Zirui Zhuang, Qi Qi, Yiming Qiu, Shinan Liu, Yunming Xiao
Web retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) splits a page into fixed-size text chunks or, in recent visual pipelines, screenshot tiles, and the retrieved item serves at once as the unit of indexing, ranking, and reading. We trace answer evidence from source HTML to reader input over the full English Wikipedia and find that this coupling loses evidence in text and screenshot pipelines alike: evidence present in the source page often fails to reach the reader intact, particularly structured content such as tables and infoboxes, which chunking separates from the headers and context that give it meaning. Stronger extraction, context expansion, and larger reader budgets leave the loss in place. We present Tessera, a training-free evidence delivery layer that decouples what a pipeline retrieves from what its reader reads. Given the pages behind any ranked list, Tessera rebuilds their HTML into fine-grained evidence units, each completed with its page title, section path, and table headers, selects the units relevant to the query, and packs them into the reader context at an unchanged token budget. The index, the retriever, and the reader stay as they are, so Tessera applies to text, screenshot, and agentic pipelines. Across three question answering benchmarks, Tessera improves answer accuracy by 5 to 6 points on text and screenshot pipelines, consistently across readers, retrievers, and reader budgets, and outperforms strong HTML-aware and structure-aware RAG baselines under matched budgets. The gains carry over to multi-step agentic search. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/sarendis56/Tessera.

☆ Compote: Collapse-Resistant Multiple Hypothesis Learning For Sequential Recommendation
Louis Castres Saint Martin, Clement Calauzenes, Alain Rakotomamonjy, Patrick Gallinari
Next-item prediction is inherently ambiguous: a single interaction history often admits multiple plausible continuations across distinct catalogue regions. Standard sequential recommenders compress these alternatives into a single prediction, conflating user intents. We introduce COllapse-resistant Multiple hyPOThesis lEarning (COMPOTE), a multi-hypothesis transformer trained with an annealed objective that transitions from uniform supervision to a winner-takes-all assignment. This mechanism forces hypotheses to specialize into distinct catalogue regions, while inference relies on an efficient, normalizer-free max-similarity rule. Theoretically, we show that in the population case, the optimal solutions partition the conditional next-item distribution according to a max-entropy quantization principle, while pooled scores preserve the Bayes-optimal ranking. We also prove a generalization bound scaling logarithmically with the number of hypotheses. Across three Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmarks, COMPOTE outperforms strong ID-based, generative, and multi-interest baselines using item IDs alone. Matched-capacity ablations confirm that performance gains stem directly from the annealed objective, preventing the head collapse observed in conventional multi-head architectures, rather than added capacity, ensembling, or routing.
☆ SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Zafer Sahinoglu, Abdulazeez Mohammed, Buse Yaren Kazangirler, Cahit Berkay Kazangirler
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems ground large language models (LLMs) by retrieving external evidence and conditioning generation on the retrieved context. Although dense retrieval is effective for local semantic matching, independently ranked retrieval can return redundant passages, miss cross-chunk dependencies, and provide incomplete evidence for multi-hop reasoning. We propose SpectRAG, a spectral graph-augmented retrieval framework that combines hybrid candidate seeding, weighted chunk graph construction, graph-based expansion, spectral relevance propagation, and token-budgeted context selection. Document chunks are represented by dense semantic embeddings and graph-spectral coordinates derived from a weighted chunk graph whose edges encode semantic similarity, document adjacency, section hierarchy, shared entities, citation links, and similarity between LLM-generated utility questions. At query time, SpectRAG builds a high-recall seed set using exact inner-product search and hybrid relevance signals, expands it over the chunk graph, re-scores candidates using graph proximity and spectral information, and assembles the final context under a fixed token budget. The goal is not merely to retrieve individually similar chunks, but to construct a context that is relevant, diverse, structurally connected, and sufficient for grounded reasoning. Experiments on MultiHopRAG, UltraDomain, and long-document question-answering settings show that SpectRAG improves broad evidence recovery and achieves competitive generation quality against dense, hybrid, HyDE, LightRAG, and NaiveRAG baselines. The results further indicate that graph-spectral structure is particularly useful for inference-oriented and cross-document retrieval, while highlighting trade-offs in early precision, computational cost, and domain-dependent performance.
